The question of whether all vegans need dietary supplements is a matter of conflicting opinions and research outcomes. Most respected and high-credibility sources assert that B12 supplementation (or fortified foods) is essential for all vegans, since "B12 is the only vitamin that is not recognised as being reliably supplied from a varied wholefood, plant-based diet" [d3]. Peer-reviewed research similarly states that "an unsupplemented diet lacks adequate amounts of a number of micronutrients and minerals that are insufficiently found in plants or may have low(er) bioavailability," and highlights the need for B12 supplements at all ages [d4], with vegans also relying on fortified foods or supplements for adequate vitamin D [d6]. However, some sources present a more conditional view: supplements for iron, calcium, and zinc are recommended only "if this can't be achieved through diet or fortified foods alone" [d1], and WebMD notes that vegans "may need a supplement" for B12 but does not state this is universal [d8]. Notably, d5 documents a conflicting viewpoint within some vegan communities — that "it's a myth that vegans need to take vitamin B12 supplements" and that "vegans can meet all of their essential nutrient needs without the use of any supplements" — though this view is characterized as a myth by most expert sources [d5]. In summary, while the mainstream expert consensus strongly recommends B12 supplementation or fortified foods for all vegans, opinions diverge on whether other supplements are universally necessary or only conditionally required [d3][d4][d6][d1][d2][d7].
